ideas.title: Lay the plank road yourself: planks are bodies, the cart thumps over your seams
ideas.goal: The player carries planks from a stack and drops them where they want the road; each plank lands on the sand by contact and rests where it settles, tilted on a hump or bridging a hollow. Then the cart drives over THEIR road: a well-laid road it rolls smoothly, a gap makes the wheel drop and thump, a plank resting on one end see-saws up and kicks the cart sideways, a steep step stalls it. Getting good at laying a road is the skill; the cart is the judge.
ideas.toward: Road steps 'wheels, axle and a wooden frame on a plank track' and 'the plank road on the dune: player lays planks' (todo #755), and the dune project, whose crest the cart can only take on a road the player laid well. It also cures what the post critic saw: wheels floating over seams.
ideas.idea: The planks and the cart become bodies in PrintSim's GPU dynamics (affine bodies with IPC contact on the island's sand heightfield): oak planks 2.2 m x 12 cm x 2 cm at 700 kg/m3, the cart's frame and four wheels as bodies joined by revolute joints, the drum motor's solved torque on the rear axle through the belt. Nothing about the road is scripted: where the wheel meets a seam, the contact decides. Someone watching sees a cart rattle over a road a player laid badly and glide over one laid well.
ideas.form: The plank carrying and dropping in Jump in, the cart on PrintSim bodies in the game; a path traced film of the cart crossing a gap and a see-sawing plank, side on and low.

ideas.title: Wind the coil by hand, the wire laid by its own tension
ideas.goal: The player turns the jig's crank and guides the copper with the other hand: guide evenly and the turns lie side by side in neat layers, guide too fast and they spiral apart with gaps, too slow and they pile into crossovers. A neat coil fits 200 turns in the space, a sloppy one 140 with a longer wire; the motor (and the cart on the planks) answers with the field THEIR coil makes. Winding is a hand skill you get better at.
ideas.toward: The human's first item, the iron stator motor (projects/fieldcoil.md): the field coil wound by Lumi's own hands, its turns and resistance measured off the simulated wire and fed to the solved FEM field and the cart.
ideas.idea: The wire is a simulated elastic rod (discrete rod in PrintSim, copper 0.8 mm, E 117 GPa) paid off a spool under the drag of a felt brake, wound onto the rotating iron core with contact against the core and the turns already laid: where each turn lands comes from tension, the guide's position and contact, not a path drawn in advance. Turns, wire length and fill are counted from the rod; motor2d's field takes the ampere-turns, the resistance takes the length. Lumi's foot holds the wire, its beak the crank (contact-held, not slid IK).
ideas.form: A winding jig on the block and a Jump in action; a close film of a neat coil and a sloppy one wound side by side, then the two carts' runs.

ideas.title: Stir the brine: a solved flow thins the tired layer
ideas.goal: After a run the cart slows because iron dissolved round the bars has piled up in a still layer. The player stirs a jar with a stick: the brine swirls, the green cloud of iron round the bar is smeared out and carried off, and that pot's volts come back. The player learns which pots to stir and how hard; an unstirred row needs ten minutes of rest.
ideas.toward: Road step 'cells that polarise' (the human's second item, cells that sag): the sag already solved in PotCell becomes a field the player sees and changes with their own hand.
ideas.idea: The jar's annulus is solved as 2D incompressible flow (a GPU grid in the horizontal cross section, the stick as a moving obstacle) with the Fe2+ concentration advected and diffused in it; the iron bar's dissolution is the flux from the motor current (Faraday) and the bar's emf takes Nernst at the concentration in the cell touching it. The green the viewer sees is that concentration field drawn as a medium in the brine.
ideas.form: A stir action in Jump in, the solved concentration drawn in the jars; a top-down traced film of a stick swirling the green away.
